Prevention: Cleaning of the crown region before the onset of monsoons.
Periodical raking of manure pit to expose larvae to predation.
Collect and destroy the various biostages of the beetle from the manure pits.
Metarhizium anisoplae in manure pits to check the perpetuation of the pest.
Monitoring: Set up light traps following the first rains in summer and monsoon period to attract the adult beetles.
Rhinolure pheromone trap at 2 traps per ha to monitor adults.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Set up light traps following the first rains in summer and monsoon period to attract and kill the adult beetles.
Rhinolure pheromone trap @ 2/2 ha to trap and kill the beetles.
Soak castor ( Ricinus communis ) cake in small mud pots and keep them in the coconut ( Cocos nucifera ) garden.
Longitudinally split tender coconut stem or fronds with fresh toddy or vinegar and keep them in the garden.
Collect and destroy the congregated beetles.
Spread neem seed powder plus sand in equal proportion on the crown region.
Trap adult beetles by keeping containers with curd + yeast + banana paste in small sachet.
Hook out and kill the adults at the crown region regularly.
For seedlings, apply 3 nos. of naphthalene balls/palm weighing 3.5 g each at the base of interspace of leaf sheath.
Baculovirus oryctes inoculated adult rhinoceros beetle reduces the leaf and crown damage caused by this beetle.
Direct Control (Chemical): Systemic with contact and stomach action
Restrictions: Highly toxic to aquatic organisms, bees, birds and mammals
